[[2007]] NCAA Tournament }} '''Daequan Cook''' is a freshman shooting guard for the [[Ohio State]] Buckeyes. ==Early Years== Born April 28, 1987, Daquean Cook is the son of Renae Cook. He has three siblings: Keishawn, Wendell, and Tauyonne. ==High School career== Daequan Cook attended [[Dunbar High School (Ohio)|Dunbar High School]] in [[Dayton, Ohio]]. As a senior, he led Dunbar to an Ohio Division II state championship. In two games at [[Value City Arena|Ohio State's Value City Arena]], he averaged 24.5 points, 6.0 rebounds, 5.0 assists, and 3.5 steals in 30.5 minutes per game. Cook earned Ohio Division II third team all-state honors as a sophomore and was a first-team selection and the Division II co-player of the year as both a junior and senior. He was named onto the 2006 [[McDonald's All-American Team]]. Playing for the West, Daequan scored 17 points, making 5 of 9 3-pointers in the win. Cook also played with [[Greg Oden]] and [[Mike Conley, Jr.]] on the SPIECE Indy Heat high school [[AAU]] team. Cook was the team's leading scorer in the 2004 Big Time event in [[Las Vegas, Nevada|Las Vegas]]. The team was undefeated and won the championship. ==College career== One of [[Ohio State University]] Coach [[Thad Matta]]'s famed "Thad Five", Cook has been averaging 10.2 points, 4.5 rebounds, 1.1 assists, and 0.7 steals in 20.4 minutes per game. Known for his pure jump shot and ability to drive to the rim, Cook is said to have the potential to be a star. On April 20, 2007, Cook announced his intentions to enter the [[2007 NBA Draft]], along with fellow freshmen teammates Oden and Conley -- though, like Conley, he has not signed with an agent.
